comparison: Perfect agreement on framework architecture and generalizability (C1, C2, C18, C22, C23, C24, C25). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes demonstration across three models and architectural clarity, while peer reviewers highlight novelty and evidence for generalization across acquisition protocols and model complexity.

Strong agreement on computational efficiency claims (C3, C16, C37, C38, C39, C60, C61). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the ~1500-fold speedup but raises concern about hardware comparison fairness (GT 710 vs RTX 4090). Peer reviewers accept computational advantages without challenge, with Reviewer 1 explicitly confirming NPE avoids repetitive forward model evaluation. Peer review also includes C19 and C62 not in OpenEval's grouping.

Strong agreement on automatic feature extraction superiority (C40, C41, C42, C51, C52, C53, C54, C55). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative improvements and methodological soundness of comparison. Peer reviewers confirm MLP captures additional information and validate improvement over state-of-the-art (Jallais et al. 2022). Peer review also includes posterior comparison claims (C34, C35, C36) not in OpenEval R3.

Strong agreement on degeneracy detection and model complexity relationship (C5, C6, C43, C44, C45, C46, C47, C48). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence from Tables 1-2 and clear definition of degeneracy measures. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight degeneracy identification as a main contribution and note it promotes analysis of degenerated nature of microstructure models. Peer review also includes C80 and C82 not in OpenEval R4.

Both address uncertainty quantification measures (C30, C31, C32, C33). OpenEval R4 groups these with degeneracy claims in a SUPPORTED evaluation. Peer R8 also finds these SUPPORTED, with reviewers acknowledging rich probabilistic information and degeneracy quantification as contributions.

Partial overlap on posterior comparison claims (C34, C35, C36). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED but notes limitation to one model and noise level. Peer R4 groups these with automatic feature extraction claims and finds all SUPPORTED, confirming superior performance to conventional approaches.

Perfect agreement on epilepsy clinical application (C49, C50, C67). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this demonstrates practical utility but cautions it's a single case without ground truth validation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept clinical application without explicit discussion or challenge.

Perfect agreement on experimental validation methodology (C20, C21, C99, C100, C102, C103, C104, C105, C106, C107, C108). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes clear specification and reproducibility. Peer reviewers explicitly validate testing across three biophysical models with community-standard data characteristics.

Perfect agreement on generalizability and limitations (C4, C56, C57, C58, C59). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative extensibility claims lacking empirical validation beyond dMRI. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, with editor noting convincing evidence for generalization across acquisition protocols, and accept author-stated limitations without challenge.

Perfect agreement on prior work citations and contextualization (C63, C64, C65, C66). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval confirms appropriate citations and positioning within literature. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge improvement over Jallais et al. (2022) as context for contribution.

Partial overlap on future applications and implications (C68, C79). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative claims lacking empirical validation (large-scale studies, acquisition optimization). Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, accepting forward-looking statements about utility without challenge. Peer R10 also includes C76, C77, C78 on uncertainty sources.

Partial overlap on uncertainty sources and model complexity discussion (C76, C77, C78). OpenEval R13 finds these SUPPORTED, noting support from demonstrated degeneracy results. Peer R10 groups these with application claims (C68, C79) and finds all SUPPORTED as discussion points and implications.

Minor overlap on degeneracy-related discussion claims (C80, C82). OpenEval R13 finds discussion claims SUPPORTED by demonstrated results. Peer R3 groups these with main degeneracy detection claims and emphasizes contribution to analyzing degenerated nature of models.

OpenEval R11 addresses background and problem context claims (C7-C17) with well-cited motivation for μGUIDE. Found SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these background claims, though they implicitly accept the motivation.

OpenEval R12 reviews alternative uncertainty quantification approaches (C69-C75) with appropriate citations. Found SUPPORTED though notes characterization could be more nuanced. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these methodological alternatives.

OpenEval R14 addresses technical background and methodological justification (C86, C87, C89-C93, C95-C97) with machine learning citations. Found SUPPORTED with logical progression from problem to solution. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this technical background.

OpenEval R15 addresses basic input-output structure description (C26, C27) shown in Figure 1. Found SUPPORTED as straightforward framework interface description. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this basic structural description.
